programmes.funder: Department of Enterprise, Tourism and Employment (administered with Enterprise Ireland)
programmes.amount_note: A €500 million challenge-based fund established under Project Ireland 2040; over €530 million has been awarded across seven calls. Call 8 has a €40 million allocation. Per-project minimum and maximum award sizes are set in each call's documentation, which had not been released at the time of checking.
programmes.deadline_note: Call 8 was announced on 9 June 2026 and will open for applications on 1 October 2026. Documentation is released closer to the opening date.

procedure_steps.detail: Form a consortium — DTIF is suitable for combinations of SMEs, MNCs and research performing organisations (RPOs).
Wait for the call documentation to be published ahead of the 1 October 2026 opening.
Submit the collaborative proposal for industrial research and/or experimental development.

documents_required.note: Documentation released closer to the call opening

eligibility.other_note: Collaborative only: consortia of SMEs, multinationals and research performing organisations engaging in industrial research and/or experimental development towards a common objective.

programmes.source_snippet: The Disruptive Technologies Innovation Fund (DTIF) is a €500 million challenge-based fund established under Project Ireland 2040 ... Call 8 was announced on 9 June 2026 and will open for applications on 1 October 2026.

programmes.amount_note: Up to 50% support on projects with total eligible costs of up to EUR 300,000, giving a maximum grant of around EUR 150,000. Designed for fast-turnaround approval (typically within weeks).
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling online applications with a fast-track approval process.

eligibility.other_note: For companies with fewer than 250 employees developing new or improved products, processes or services on a short timeline. Enterprise Ireland client status generally required.

programmes.amount_note: Three strands: Commercial Case Feasibility (up to around EUR 15,000), Commercialisation Fund Projects (typically EUR 100,000-350,000) and larger projects up to around EUR 650,000 for spin-out ready technologies.
programmes.deadline_note: Runs to published call deadlines, historically two or three a year.

eligibility.other_note: Applications come from researchers in Irish higher education institutes and research performing organisations, not from companies. It is the main route to an Irish university spin-out.

programmes.amount_note: Historically EUR 50,000 for a 10% ordinary equity stake, awarded through competitive themed calls (including women-only, graduate and sector strands).
programmes.deadline_note: Ran as themed competitive calls several times a year until it was retired.
programmes.reopen_note: Discontinued and replaced by the Pre-Seed Start Fund, which serves the same early-stage segment with EUR 50,000 or EUR 100,000 investments. Apply to the Pre-Seed Start Fund instead.

programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 150,000 to support digital transformation of business processes.
programmes.source_snippet: Digital Process Innovation - Up to EUR 150,000

programmes.amount_note: Enterprise Ireland runs a family of female entrepreneurship supports (Empower Start, Level Up, Innovate) providing training, mentoring and in some strands a stipend or grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Programme cohorts recruit once or twice a year.
programmes.reopen_note: Enterprise Ireland's Action Plan for Women in Business commits to continued female founder programmes; check the Enterprise Ireland women in business pages for the current cohort call.

eligibility.other_note: Enterprise Ireland also ring-fences a female-founder strand within the Pre-Seed Start Fund.

programmes.amount_note: National funding for Irish participants in Eurostars and Eureka transnational R&D projects, at Enterprise Ireland RD&I grant rates.
programmes.deadline_note: Follows the Eurostars international cut-offs, typically twice a year in spring and autumn.

programmes.amount_note: Salary support towards employing graduates, historically up to 50-70% of salary costs for up to two years (higher rates in the regions and for graduates with modern languages).
programmes.deadline_note: Runs as annual calls with a defined application window.
programmes.reopen_note: GradStart has run in annual cycles; check the Enterprise Ireland supports pages for the current call window.

programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 50,000 each for structured sustainability (GreenPlus) or operational excellence (LeanPlus) improvement projects, typically at 50% of eligible consultancy and training costs.

eligibility.other_note: Enterprise Ireland also runs smaller Lean Start and Green Start supports for first steps.

programmes.source_snippet: LeanPlus - Up to EUR 50,000 ... GreenPlus - Up to EUR 50,000

programmes.amount_note: Grant towards researching market opportunity and preparing a business plan for a High Potential Start-Up. Historically up to around EUR 15,000 at 50% of eligible costs.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling, through an Enterprise Ireland HPSU adviser.

eligibility.other_note: For entrepreneurs with a HPSU-eligible proposition (exportable, innovative, potential for EUR 1m sales and 10 jobs within 3 years).

programmes.amount_note: Enterprise Ireland funds up to 80% of the eligible cost of a collaborative research project between a company and an Irish research institution (up to 50% for large companies). The company pays the balance.

eligibility.other_note: Company gains favourable access to the resulting IP. Available to companies of any size based in Ireland, including non-EI clients.

programmes.amount_note: Standard vouchers worth EUR 10,000; co-funded vouchers up to EUR 20,000 (the company contributes part of the cost). Vouchers are valid for 18 months.
programmes.deadline_note: Available all year round - no call windows.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify a registered knowledge provider (Irish or approved overseas higher education institute or research body)
Apply online for the voucher
Voucher issued; agree the project with the knowledge provider
Knowledge provider delivers and redeems the voucher

documents_required.doc: Description of the innovation question or challenge

eligibility.other_note: Open to limited companies registered in Ireland. Cannot be used for routine consultancy or for work the company could do itself. One of the easiest entry points into the Irish innovation funding system.

programmes.source_snippet: Standard vouchers worth EUR 10,000 ... co-funded vouchers up to EUR 20,000 ... all vouchers are valid for 18 months and available all year round.

programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 1.2 million of equity co-investment into High Potential Start-Ups, matched with private investment. Delivered in tranches as the company hits milestones.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling, through an assigned Enterprise Ireland HPSU development adviser.

eligibility.other_note: Requires matching private investment. The company must be designated a High Potential Start-Up by Enterprise Ireland.

programmes.source_snippet: Innovative HPSU Fund - Up to EUR 1,200,000

programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 150,000 towards the salary cost of recruiting a senior manager with skills the company lacks, typically over two to three years on a tapering basis.

eligibility.other_note: For Enterprise Ireland client companies; the role must be genuinely additional.

programmes.source_snippet: Key Manager Support - Up to EUR 150,000

programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 35,000 towards market research to support an export growth plan.
programmes.source_snippet: Market Research Grant - Up to EUR 35,000

programmes.funder: Enterprise Ireland (delivered by Institutes of Technology / Technological Universities)
programmes.amount_note: Phase 2 participants receive a scholarship/stipend of around EUR 15,000 over six months, plus free incubation space, mentoring and training. Phases 1 and 3 are unpaid but provide training and support.
programmes.deadline_note: Each delivery institution runs its own recruitment, typically once or twice a year.

procedure_steps.detail: Choose a New Frontiers delivery location (there are hubs across Ireland)
Apply to that hub's current intake
Phase 1: part-time evening idea validation
Phase 2: full-time six-month programme with stipend
Phase 3: post-programme support and investor readiness

eligibility.other_note: Applicants must be able to commit full-time in Phase 2 and be developing an innovative, exportable business. National programme delivered locally, so check each hub's calendar.

programmes.name_local: New Markets Validation Grant (formerly Market Discovery Fund)
programmes.name_en: New Markets Validation Grant (formerly Market Discovery Fund)
programmes.amount_note: Up to EUR 150,000 towards researching and validating new export markets. Support is tiered by project size with a co-funding requirement.

eligibility.other_note: For Enterprise Ireland clients pursuing new geographic markets or new market segments.

programmes.source_snippet: New Markets Validation Grant - Up to EUR 150,000

programmes.amount_note: Investment of either EUR 50,000 or EUR 100,000 into early-stage companies, plus 10 structured mentoring sessions.
programmes.deadline_note: Runs to periodic calls with distinct strands, historically including a general strand and dedicated female-founder and regional strands.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the company meets Enterprise Ireland's HPSU criteria (exporting, scalable, innovative)
Discuss with an Enterprise Ireland adviser or a Local Enterprise Office
Submit the application in an open call window
Assessment and investment committee decision
Investment agreement and mentoring assignment

documents_required.doc: Evidence of matching private investment where required

eligibility.other_note: Replaced the Competitive Start Fund. For manufacturing or internationally traded services companies with export potential. Requires matching private investment in most strands.

programmes.source_snippet: Funding and supports for early-stage companies ... 10 mentoring sessions ... investment of either EUR 50,000 or EUR 100,000.

programmes.amount_note: Support for substantial in-company R&D projects. Grant rates follow EU State aid limits - typically up to 45-50% for small enterprises on industrial research, lower for experimental development and large companies.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling; larger projects go to Enterprise Ireland's investment committee.

eligibility.other_note: For Enterprise Ireland client companies with significant R&D ambition. Projects typically run 12-36 months.

programmes.amount_note: Large competitive fund for regional enterprise innovation infrastructure and collaborative projects; awards typically in the hundreds of thousands to several million.
programmes.deadline_note: Runs as competitive calls with defined windows.
programmes.reopen_note: Successor to the Regional Enterprise Development Fund and Regional Enterprise Transition Scheme; Enterprise Ireland has run regional competitive calls repeatedly. Watch the Enterprise Ireland supports page for the next call.

eligibility.other_note: Applicants are usually consortia, clusters and enterprise infrastructure projects rather than individual startups.

programmes.funder: European Space Agency (ESA) with the national space agency or regional co-funder
programmes.amount_note: EUR 50,000 equity-free funding for product and IP development, plus up to two years of incubation with technical support from ESA experts, business coaching, legal and IPR advice and fundraising support. Some national BICs add local top-up funding.
programmes.deadline_note: This ESA BIC runs its own call cycle with published cut-off dates, typically two to four per year. Contact the local centre for the next deadline.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact the local ESA BIC to discuss suitability
Submit application documents before the local deadline
Tender Opening Board review, then presentation to the Tender Evaluation Board
Register a company in Ireland before signing the incubation contract

eligibility.other_note: Business must use space-based systems, apply space technology in a non-space domain, or develop products and services for the space sector. Company must be registered in Ireland.

programmes.source_snippet: €50k equity free funding for product and IP development

programmes.name_en: Enterprise Ireland HPSU Feasibility Study Grant
programmes.amount_note: Maximum award: €30,000. The percentage of eligible costs covered was not stated on the page read.
programmes.deadline_note: No published deadline; applied for through your Enterprise Ireland development adviser.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm you are an existing Enterprise Ireland client and an innovative HPSU preparing to raise investment.
Agree the scope of the feasibility work with your Enterprise Ireland adviser and apply.
Use the grant to prepare an investor-ready business plan.

eligibility.other_note: Restricted to innovative HPSUs preparing to raise investment who are existing Enterprise Ireland clients.

programmes.source_snippet: Maximum award: €30,000 ... Innovative HPSUs preparing to raise investment, who is an existing Enterprise Ireland client. ... Prepare an investor-ready business plan.

programmes.name_en: IDA Ireland funding programmes and incentives
programmes.amount_note: Individual award sizes are negotiated per investment and are not published. IDA operates a €100m annual capital grant programme for supporting investment projects, with grant levels depending on company size and investment impact; RD&I is the largest proportion of IDA's grant funding programme. Grant aid is also available for in-house bespoke training and management mentoring, business asset grants, lean/digitalisation and sustainability. Ireland's 25% R&D tax credit is cited separately by IDA (note: Revenue confirms 30% for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024, so IDA's page appears out of date on this point).
programmes.deadline_note: No calls; IDA's Board meets every month to make decisions on supporting company investments, in strict compliance with EU state aid rules.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact IDA Ireland to discuss the proposed investment in Ireland.
Develop a project proposal with an IDA executive covering capital, employment, RD&I, training or sustainability elements.
Proposal goes to IDA's independent Board of Directors, which meets monthly to decide on support.

documents_required.note: Developed with an IDA executive; format not published

eligibility.other_note: IDA Ireland is the foreign direct investment agency: support is aimed at overseas-owned companies investing or expanding in Ireland, not at indigenous startups (which are served by Enterprise Ireland and the Local Enterprise Offices). Decisions are made in strict compliance with EU state aid rules.

programmes.source_snippet: €100m annual grant programme for supporting investment projects ... RD&I is the largest proportion of IDA's grant funding programme ... Grant aid available for in-house bespoke training and management mentoring

programmes.name_local: IDA Ireland RD&I and capital grants
programmes.name_en: IDA Ireland RD&I and capital grants
programmes.amount_note: Employment, capital, training, and RD&I grants negotiated per project against EU State aid limits. Typically for foreign-owned companies investing in Ireland.

eligibility.other_note: IDA supports foreign direct investment into Ireland. Irish-owned startups go to Enterprise Ireland or their LEO instead. IDA can be relevant to an overseas startup opening an Irish operation.

programmes.amount_note: Standard vouchers are worth €10,000. Co-Funded Vouchers are worth up to €20,000, where the company contributes part of the cost. All vouchers are valid for 18 months.
programmes.deadline_note: Available all year round.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify a registered knowledge provider (Irish or approved) to work with on a specific business challenge.
Apply online for the voucher.
Redeem the voucher with the knowledge provider within its 18-month validity period.

documents_required.note: Describes the innovation question and the chosen knowledge provider

eligibility.other_note: Open to Irish-registered SMEs seeking innovative input from a registered knowledge provider. Not restricted to Enterprise Ireland clients.

programmes.source_snippet: SMEs seeking innovative input; Standard €10K vouchers; Co-Funded Vouchers up to €20,000; All vouchers are valid for 18 months and available all year round.

programmes.name_en: Enterprise Ireland Innovative High Potential Start-Up Fund
programmes.amount_note: The iHPSU page states 'Up to €1.2 million' in its at-a-glance panel, while Enterprise Ireland's startup landing page describes 'co-funded equity investment of up to €800,000'. Both figures appear on Enterprise Ireland's own site; treat €800,000 as the commonly quoted headline and €1.2m as the stated upper bound, and confirm with EI before relying on either. Co-funding model: Enterprise Ireland does not lead investment rounds and requires external investment to be raised first.
programmes.deadline_note: No published deadline; engagement is via Enterprise Ireland's High Potential Start-Up Unit and is tied to the company's private investment round.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm you meet the HPSU definition and engage with Enterprise Ireland's HPSU Unit.
Raise external private investment — Enterprise Ireland co-invests and does not lead rounds.
Submit a business plan and financial projections for appraisal.
If approved, Enterprise Ireland takes an equity stake alongside the private investors.

documents_required.note: An HPSU Feasibility Study Grant of up to €30,000 is available to existing EI clients to prepare it

eligibility.other_note: A High Potential Start-Up is defined as introducing a new product or service to international markets that is truly innovative and disruptive with some form of protectable IP; involved in manufacturing or internationally traded services; capable of creating 10 jobs in Ireland and €1 million in annual sales within three years of starting; led by an experienced management team residing in Ireland; headquartered and controlled in Ireland; and less than five years old from the date of company registration. Must have an MVP and some commercial traction.

programmes.source_snippet: Capable of creating 10 jobs in Ireland and realising €1 million in annual sales within three years of starting ... Less than five years old from the date of your company's registration ... Enterprise Ireland's iHPSU fund operates on a co-funding model. We do not lead on investment rounds

programmes.name_en: Local Enterprise Office Business Expansion Grant
programmes.admin_area: Ireland — delivered by 31 Local Enterprise Offices
programmes.funder: Local Enterprise Office (Enterprise Ireland / local authorities)
programmes.amount_note: Maximum 50% of the investment or, in exceptional circumstances, €150,000 — whichever is the lesser. Salary support capped at €15,000 per full-time job created, subject to the 50% limit.
programmes.deadline_note: Ongoing assessment by the local LEO evaluation committee.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your Local Enterprise Office to confirm eligibility (past the initial 18-month start-up period).
Prepare a growth plan with costed investment and job creation projections.
Submit the application to the LEO evaluation committee.

eligibility.other_note: For businesses employing up to 10 staff in the growth phase after the initial 18-month start-up period. Covers capital development, equipment, utilities, salary support, consultancy, innovation and marketing. Retail, personal services, professional services, construction and local services are ineligible.

programmes.source_snippet: The Business Expansion Grant is designed to assist businesses, employing up to 10 staff in its growth phase after the initial 18-month start-up period. The maximum Business Expansion Grant payable must not exceed 50% of the investment or, in exceptional circumstances, €150,000 - or whichever is the lesser.

programmes.amount_note: Up to 75% of eligible costs to a maximum of around EUR 5,000, towards technical assessments and capital equipment that reduce energy use.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling within annual budget.

eligibility.other_note: Open to a wider set of sectors than the core LEO grants, including retail and hospitality in most counties. Confirm with your LEO.

programmes.name_en: Local Enterprise Office Feasibility Study Grant
programmes.admin_area: Ireland — delivered by 31 Local Enterprise Offices
programmes.funder: Local Enterprise Office (Enterprise Ireland / local authorities)
programmes.amount_note: 50% of investment in the South and East Region and 60% in the Border, Midlands and West Region, up to a maximum of €15,000 (whichever is the lesser). Own labour is claimable at a maximum of €400 per week and not exceeding 20% of the grant.
programmes.deadline_note: Ongoing assessment by the local LEO.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your Local Enterprise Office and scope the feasibility work.
Submit an application setting out the market research, technical development or prototype work planned.

eligibility.other_note: Supports research of market demand for a product or service and examination of its sustainability. Covers market research, consultancy fees, technical development, prototype creation and own labour. Retail, personal services, professional services, construction and local services are ineligible.

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum Feasibility Study Grant is from 50% (in the South and East Region) to 60% (in the Borders Midlands, West Region) of investment and up to a maximum of €15,000, whichever is the lesser.

programmes.amount_note: Typically 50% of eligible costs up to a maximum of around EUR 15,000 (some LEOs apply a lower cap). Covers market research, prototype development, consultancy and technical feasibility.

eligibility.other_note: Caps vary slightly between LEOs - confirm with your own county office. Enterprise must employ no more than 10 people including the owner, be established, registered and operating in that LEO's county, and be a manufacturing, internationally traded services, or domestically traded business with international growth potential. LEOs cannot support retail, wholesale, personal services, professional services, construction, accommodation or agriculture. There are 31 Local Enterprise Offices, one in each local authority area - apply to the LEO for the county where you are based.

programmes.admin_area: Ireland — delivered by 31 Local Enterprise Offices
programmes.funder: Local Enterprise Office (Enterprise Ireland / local authorities)
programmes.amount_note: Maximum 50% of the investment up to €80,000; the LEO can approve up to €150,000 in certain/exceptional situations. Salary costs are supported at a maximum of €15,000 per full-time job created, subject to the 50% limit.
programmes.deadline_note: Applications assessed by the local LEO on an ongoing basis, typically via an evaluation committee.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your Local Enterprise Office to discuss eligibility.
Prepare a business plan with costed investment and job creation projections.
Submit the application to the LEO evaluation committee.

documents_required.doc: Financial projections and quotes for capital items

eligibility.other_note: A business start-up grant for micro enterprises employing up to 10 employees, within 18 months of starting. Eligible costs include capital items, equipment, utilities, salary costs (max €15,000 per job), consultancy, innovation and marketing. Retail, personal services, professional services, construction and local services are ineligible.

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum Priming Grant payable must not exceed 50% of the investment up to €80,000 but the LEO can approve up to €150,000 in certain situations.

programmes.amount_note: Matched funding of up to 50% of eligible export marketing costs, to a maximum of around EUR 2,500. Covers trade fair participation, international marketing material, translation and export consultancy.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling but budget-limited; some LEOs run annual calls that close when funds are exhausted.

eligibility.other_note: Must be approved before the expenditure is incurred. Enterprise must employ no more than 10 people including the owner, be established, registered and operating in that LEO's county, and be a manufacturing, internationally traded services, or domestically traded business with international growth potential. LEOs cannot support retail, wholesale, personal services, professional services, construction, accommodation or agriculture. There are 31 Local Enterprise Offices, one in each local authority area - apply to the LEO for the county where you are based.

programmes.funder: Local Enterprise Offices / Department of the Environment, Climate and Communications
programmes.amount_note: Voucher of up to EUR 2,500 with 50% co-funding by the business, towards developing or upgrading an e-commerce website, digital marketing or online payments.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling, but you must attend a Trading Online Voucher information seminar before applying, and budgets are annual.

procedure_steps.detail: Attend a free Trading Online Voucher information seminar run by your LEO
Get two or three quotations from web developers or digital suppliers
Submit the voucher application
Approval, then complete the work and claim

eligibility.other_note: Business must have fewer than 10 employees, turnover under EUR 2 million, and be trading for at least six months. Retail businesses ARE eligible for this voucher (unlike most LEO grants).

programmes.amount_note: Unsecured business loans from EUR 5,000 to EUR 25,000 over terms of up to five years. Reduced interest rate for applicants referred by a Local Enterprise Office.

procedure_steps.detail: Try your bank first - MFI requires evidence you were declined or could not get suitable credit
Apply directly or, for a lower rate, through your Local Enterprise Office
Credit assessment
Loan offer and drawdown

documents_required.doc: Evidence of bank refusal or unsuitable terms

eligibility.other_note: For businesses with fewer than 10 employees and turnover under EUR 2 million. Unlike most LEO supports, all sectors including retail and services are eligible. You normally need to show you could not get bank finance.

programmes.amount_note: Investment of €50,000 or €100,000, released in tranches. The first €50,000 tranche is released subject to the company confirming an additional new cash co-investment of a minimum of €5,000. Includes 10 mentoring sessions. Former Competitive Start Fund investee companies may apply for a maximum of €50,000 if suitable.
programmes.deadline_note: Run as competitive calls. Specific call dates were not visible on the page read; check the Enterprise Ireland support page for the current call. The Pre-Seed Start Fund is Enterprise Ireland's current early-stage equity offering — the older Competitive Start Fund (CSF) is referenced only historically, with former CSF investees eligible for up to €50,000.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm you are an existing or potential client of Enterprise Ireland's High Potential Start-Up Unit with evidence of innovation, internationalisation potential and employment capacity.
Apply during an open call.
If successful, secure the minimum €5,000 new cash co-investment to release the first €50,000 tranche.

documents_required.doc: Evidence of new cash co-investment of at least €5,000
documents_required.note: Condition of releasing the first tranche

eligibility.other_note: Requires evidence of innovation, internationalisation potential and employment capacity, and status as an existing or potential Enterprise Ireland HPSU client.

programmes.source_snippet: Former Competitive Start Fund (CSF) investee companies may apply for a maximum of €50,000 if they are suitable. ... The first €50,000 tranche will be released to successful applicants subject to the company providing confirmation that an additional new cash co-investment of a minimum of €5,000.

programmes.name_en: Irish Research and Development (R&D) Corporation Tax Credit
programmes.amount_note: 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure for accounting periods commencing on or after 1 January 2024 (previously 25%). The credit is repaid in three annual instalments; for each instalment the company elects whether it is treated as an overpayment, offset against tax liabilities, or repaid in cash. No cap on qualifying expenditure.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed in the corporation tax return; claims must generally be made within 12 months of the end of the accounting period.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the activities meet the statutory definition of qualifying R&D and record qualifying expenditure.
Claim the credit in the corporation tax return (Form CT1) for the accounting period.
Elect for each of the three annual instalments how it should be treated (offset or repaid).

documents_required.doc: Form CT1 corporation tax return with R&D claim
Contemporaneous technical and financial records of the R&D
documents_required.note: Required to support the claim on Revenue audit

eligibility.other_note: Available to companies within the charge to Irish corporation tax carrying out qualifying R&D in Ireland or the EEA. The credit is repayable in cash even for loss-making companies, which makes it materially useful for pre-revenue startups.

programmes.source_snippet: For accounting periods commencing on or after 1 January 2024, the rate has increased to 30%.

programmes.amount_note: A qualifying company can raise up to EUR 5.5 million a year and EUR 16.5 million in its lifetime. Investors get income tax relief on their investment, making the round easier to raise.

eligibility.other_note: Self-assessed by the company - there is no advance approval, so professional advice is essential. Shares must be held for at least four years by the investor.

programmes.amount_note: Refundable credit on qualifying R&D expenditure. The rate was increased to 30% (from 25%) for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024. Payable in three instalments, or in full in year one below a first-year payment threshold.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed with the corporation tax return; the claim must be made within 12 months of the end of the accounting period in which the expenditure was incurred - a hard deadline with no extension.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify qualifying R&D activities under the science and technology test
Track qualifying expenditure (staff, materials, plant, subcontracting within limits)
Prepare technical and financial documentation contemporaneously
File the claim with the CT1 return within 12 months of the period end
Revenue may raise queries or audit

documents_required.doc: Technical report describing the scientific or technological uncertainty and advance

eligibility.other_note: The single most valuable non-dilutive support for Irish R&D startups because it is refundable in cash even when loss-making. The 12-month claim deadline is strict. Grant funding must be deducted from qualifying expenditure.

programmes.name_local: Start-up companies relief from corporation tax (Section 486C)
programmes.name_en: Start-up companies relief from corporation tax (Section 486C)
programmes.amount_note: Relief from corporation tax for the first five years of trading. Full relief where corporation tax due is EUR 40,000 or less in the year, with marginal relief up to EUR 60,000. Capped by reference to employer PRSI paid.

eligibility.other_note: Claimed in the corporation tax return. Only relevant once profitable, but it can be carried forward if unused in the first five years.

programmes.amount_note: Refund of PAYE income tax paid over the previous six years, invested into your own new company. Refund can be up to around EUR 140,000 depending on prior tax paid (up to EUR 100,000 per year invested).

eligibility.other_note: You must have been mainly in PAYE employment, take up full-time employment in the new company as a director, and hold at least 15% of the shares. Powerful for a first-time founder leaving a salaried job.

programmes.name_local: Screen Ireland / Fís Éireann development funding
programmes.name_en: Screen Ireland development and production funding
programmes.amount_note: Development loans and production funding for Irish film, television and animation, plus separate schemes for emerging talent. Amounts are set per scheme in the published guidelines.
programmes.deadline_note: Schemes have individual deadlines published on the Screen Ireland funding pages; some development funding is assessed on a rolling basis.

eligibility.other_note: Irish-registered production companies. Ireland's Section 481 tax credit is a separate, complementary instrument.

programmes.name_local: SEAI Research, Development and Demonstration Fund
programmes.name_en: SEAI Research, Development and Demonstration Fund
programmes.amount_note: Supports energy RD&D projects. Awards have ranged from tens of thousands for feasibility to around EUR 1 million for demonstration projects; grant rates follow State aid limits.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual competitive call, historically opening in the autumn or winter with a several-week window.
programmes.reopen_note: The SEAI RD&D Fund has run annually since 2018. Expect the next call to open around the autumn - check the SEAI research funding page.

eligibility.other_note: Open to companies, research organisations and public bodies in Ireland. Projects must have a clear Irish energy system benefit.

programmes.name_local: Research Ireland (SFI) Frontiers for the Future
programmes.name_en: Research Ireland (SFI) Frontiers for the Future
programmes.amount_note: Projects strand typically up to around EUR 450,000 direct costs; Programme strand larger, up to around EUR 1 million or more over four to five years.
programmes.deadline_note: Annual call cycle with a pre-proposal stage.

eligibility.other_note: Academic research funding - the pipeline that feeds Irish deeptech spinouts. Science Foundation Ireland and the Irish Research Council merged into Research Ireland in 2024.

programmes.amount_note: Funds an academic researcher to spend up to 12-24 months embedded in a company (or vice versa), covering salary and related costs.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling submission in most years.

eligibility.other_note: A cheap way for an Irish startup to get research capacity. The host institution applies with the company as partner.

programmes.amount_note: Capital, employment, feasibility, R&D and training grants for businesses in Gaeltacht areas. Amounts negotiated per project within EU State aid limits; feasibility grants are typically small (tens of thousands) and capital grants can be substantially larger.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications through an Udaras regional office.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your regional Udaras na Gaeltachta office
Discuss the project and eligibility with a development executive
Submit a business plan and grant application
Board approval
Draw down against evidenced spend

eligibility.other_note: The business must be located in a Gaeltacht area (parts of Donegal, Mayo, Galway, Kerry, Cork, Meath and Waterford). Udaras is the enterprise agency for these areas in place of Enterprise Ireland and the LEOs, and also operates gteic digital hubs.
